cells.tense: The gathering is happening now, and you are holding the pen while it does.
cells.ask: Write down the three threads you're carrying and pick the one that goes first this week. The other two stay on the page, not in your head.
cells.core:
You're collecting the loose pieces right now — the half-thoughts, the conversation you keep replaying, the thing you almost decided. You're pulling them into one line that makes sense, and the pulling has your hand on it. That's not a small thing. Scattered stays scattered for a lot of people.

The fairness part is quiet and working. You can feel which version of events is true without grinding through the arithmetic of who owes what. That felt-sense is doing the gathering, and it's why the line you draw tends to hold. When it's like this, you don't need to check it twice. The thing to feed is the next thing — one more piece gathered while the ease is here, before the week fills up again.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a moment that hasn't arrived and can't be written in ahead of time.
cells.ask: Close the notebook on the parts of this you can't decide yet. Do one thing today that only needs today's version of the answer.
cells.core:
You're trying to gather everything at once, and you're gathering it for a future you keep rehearsing. Loose ends get pulled into the plan before they're ripe, and talks get their endings written in advance. You're not scattered — you're over-collected, forcing a final shape onto thoughts that are still arriving.

The cost is that nothing gets to land. You keep pushing for the version where it's all resolved, and that push is standing in for the living. There's a simpler motion available: let the feeling pick the direction, then move. You don't have to have the whole line mapped. One honest step today does more than the entire strategy you're drafting for a moment that keeps not coming.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, and the floor there is familiar.
cells.ask: Say one true sentence out loud to someone about how you actually feel, no summary or plan attached. Then stop and let it sit.
cells.core:
Nothing is being pulled into anything. The thoughts are still there, dropped where they landed, and you don't reach for them. The standing-still is real, and it's where you are now.

More thinking isn't the move. It's the felt thing underneath — the recognition of what you actually hold, without fusing it with anyone else's version. That kind of knowing is quiet and it doesn't need an audience. When it's working, you can sit with what your heart already knows and still be in the room with another person. Start there. One honest sentence, said to one person, is the whole first move.
cells.sheetLine: The thoughts are still there. You stopped reaching for them.

cells.tense: You are already gathering the pieces into a line, but you're calling it something that's just happening.
cells.ask: Tell one person the version of this you've worked out, in your own words, and let them hear you say it.
cells.core:
The work is underway — collecting the loose ends, finding the thread that makes them one thing, deciding what it adds up to. You describe it as the situation sorting itself out, as if the shape arrived on its own. It didn't. The shape came from your hands.

What's left is naming that out loud. And there's something older you know how to do: put what you've come to understand where someone else can take it in and carry it. That's not performance. That's how meaning travels between people. The finished thought has stayed private. One telling, to one person, is the whole move — and it makes the gathering yours.
cells.sheetLine: The gathering is yours, and it stays private until it's told.

attempts.check: The medicine cards' faces (Conscience, Alignment, Reverie, Celebration) are record facts, but rendering them too literally risks reading as a second card being prescribed rather than a posture the person already has. The reader could say 'I'm not feeling unfair or celebratory, I'm just trying to get my head straight' — the asks survive that, because each is a small visible act around gathering what's already there, not a demand to feel something. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line about 'alignment' or 'harvest' as if the person should already know the vocabulary; it's cut.
